scenario: [LERR.1.4.12]: a pair that ends and is later derived again records again. Asserting `c1` (key k2, `y = 0`) derives `((a1), c1)` at the join `c.x / c.y > 1.0`, which traps (an all-Int division [LEXP.7.15.1]): one ComputationError. Asserting `b1` (a1's key, `y = 1`) blocks `(a1)` at the NOT node and ends the pair; its own pair `((a1), b1)` answers `false` and records nothing. Retracting `b1` releases `(a1)`, which derives `((a1), c1)` again ([IRET.7.9.3]), and it traps again, after the retraction ([RFCS.6.7]). Two ComputationErrors in all, and only one fact retraction. PATH: libds records each at the end of the event that derived it (rete/beta.c ds_rete_beta_flush_match_traps); Mercury in ds.match.lerr_1_4_12_derived. The runtime differential runs the same program (114_rederived_trap). `r` does not fire.
